So the valence electrons are the electrons in the outermost shell, which are 3s² and 3p⁴. Adding those together gives 2 + 4 = 6 valence electrons. 

Wait, but sometimes I get confused between group number and valence electrons. Group 16 elements have six valence electrons because the group number is equal to the number of valence electrons for elements in that group. So oxygen has six, sulfur has six, and selenium should also have six.

Let me double-check that. The periodic table groups are arranged based on the number of valence electrons. Group 1 has 1, Group 2 has 2, and so on. So Group 16 should have 6 valence electrons. Yeah, that makes sense. 

I think I might have made a mistake earlier when I thought it was five. Maybe I was mixing up the number of valence electrons with something else. No, wait, oxygen has six, so selenium should too. I'm confident now that the correct answer is 6, which is option C.
